title: manage ai settings / Use {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} device policies
content:
## Use {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} device policies The following sections describe {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} device policies. Deploy them by following [Enterprise policies](/docs/enterprise/policies.md), and use the [policy reference](/docs/enterprise/policies.md#vs-code-enterprise-policy-reference) for accepted values and minimum versions. > [!IMPORTANT] > {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} harness sessions don't enforce every device policy the same way as Local harness sessions. The following sections note known differences. Test a policy in the harness that your developers use before you rely on it. Jump to: * [Control access and feature availability](#control-access-and-feature-availability) * [Configure models and data handling](#configure-models-and-data-handling) * [Govern agents and tools](#govern-agents-and-tools) * [Configure security and observability](#configure-security-and-observability) ### Control access and feature availability #### Restrict AI features to approved GitHub organizations Set the `ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations` policy to require developers to sign in with a GitHub account that belongs to an approved organization before AI features are activated. Provide a JSON array of GitHub organization logins, such as `["contoso", "contoso-research"]`. Use `["*"]` to allow any signed-in GitHub account. The policy is fail-closed. AI features remain disabled until account policy data resolves and the signed-in account belongs to an approved organization. Run **Developer: Policy Diagnostics** to inspect the **Account Policy Gate** state. #### Enable or disable the use of agents Set the `ChatAgentMode` policy to `false` to disable [agents](/docs/agents/overview.md). This policy controls `setting(chat.agent.enabled)`. When the policy is disabled, the **Agent** option is not available in the agents dropdown, and the {% data variables.copilot.agents_window %} is unavailable. Developers can still use [ask or edit](/docs/chat/chat-overview.md) for code explanations and file edits. The policy does not remove Agent Host session targets, such as **Copilot**, from the [**Session Target** UI control](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#select-a-harness) in the editor. Developers can still start agent sessions from those targets. #### Enable or disable extension language tools Use the following policies to control extension, browser, and plugin tools: * Set `ChatAgentExtensionTools` to `false` to disable tools contributed by extensions. * Set `BrowserChatTools` to `false` to disable browser tools. * Set `ChatPluginsEnabled` to `false` to disable agent plugin integration. #### Configure {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} code review Use `CopilotReviewSelection` to control code review for selected code. Use `CopilotReviewAgent` to control access to the code review agent for pull requests and changed files. #### Configure next edit suggestions Set `CopilotNextEditSuggestions` to `false` to disable next edit suggestions. #### Enable or disable Claude Agent Set `Claude3PIntegration` to `false` to disable Claude Agent sessions in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}. Setting this policy to `true` does not override the [Claude and Codex restriction under enterprise-managed settings](#claude-and-codex-availability). #### Enable or disable the copilot command {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} includes a `copilot` command that runs {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cli %}. When {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cli_short %} isn't installed, the command offers to install it from GitHub. On Windows, setup can also [add the command to `PATH` and install {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cli_short %}](/docs/setup/windows.md#set-up-the-copilot-command). Set the `CopilotCliCommand` policy to `false` to turn off the command. This policy controls `setting(chat.copilotCliCommand.enabled)`. When the policy is disabled: * New integrated terminals don't include the `copilot` command. * On Windows, setup doesn't show its **{% data variables.copilot.copilot_cli %}** page or install {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cli_short %}. The next time setup runs, for example during an update, it removes the `copilot` command from `PATH`. Until then, the command doesn't install {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cli_short %}. The policy doesn't affect a {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cli_short %} installation that you deploy separately. To control which {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cli_short %} version developers use and where it comes from, disable the policy and deploy {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cli_short %} with your own software distribution tools. Learn more about [installing {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cli %}](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/set-up-copilot-cli/install-copilot-cli). Whether developers can use {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cli_short %} is controlled by your [GitHub organization and enterprise settings](#use-github-organization-and-enterprise-settings), which {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cli_short %} applies after sign-in. ### Configure models and data handling #### Set a default chat model Set the `ChatDefaultModel` policy to choose the default model for new conversations. This policy controls `setting(chat.defaultModel)` and accepts `auto`, a model family name, or a full model ID. Developers can select another model for an individual conversation. Reopened conversations keep their saved model. For defaults delivered through {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} enterprise-managed settings, see [Set managed model defaults](#set-managed-model-defaults). #### Control dictation data Use the following policies to control whether [dictation](/docs/configure/accessibility/voice.md#use-built-in-dictation) audio and transcripts leave the developer's device. | Policy | Setting | Behavior | |--------|---------|----------| | `DictationEnabled` | `setting(dictation.enabled)` | Controls whether built-in dictation is available. | | `DictationModel` | `setting(dictation.model)` | Selects an on-device model or the `mai` cloud transcription service. | | `DictationLLMCleanup` | `setting(dictation.experimental.llmCleanup)` | Controls whether final transcripts are sent to a language model for cleanup. | To keep dictation audio on the device, set `DictationModel` to `nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b`. In {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} for the Web, where on-device transcription is not supported, this policy makes dictation unavailable. To prevent transcript text from being sent to a language model, set `DictationLLMCleanup` to `false`. For more information, see [Dictation privacy](/docs/configure/accessibility/voice.md#understand-dictation-privacy). ### Govern agents and tools #### Enable or disable hooks Hook controls depend on the selected harness. For {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} harness sessions, use [Policy Hooks](#verify-policy-hook-coverage) and the [managed hook-source controls](#restrict-hook-sources) below. > [!NOTE] > **For Local harness sessions:** Set the `ChatHooks` policy to `false` to disable hooks. This policy controls `setting(chat.useHooks)` and does not apply to {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} harness sessions. ##### Verify Policy Hook coverage {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} Policy Hooks apply to Copilot harness sessions, which use the {% data variables.copilot.copilot_sdk_short %} hook implementation. Confirm that developers select **Copilot** from the [**Session Target** UI control](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#select-a-harness) before relying on these hooks for enforcement. Test the required hook behavior in the session that will perform the work. Local harness sessions do not load SDK Policy Hooks. Configuring hooks for one harness does not enforce them in another harness. See [hook compatibility](/docs/agent-customization/hooks.md#choose-the-hook-implementation-for-your-session). When moving to Copilot, inventory policy hooks, managed plugins, and any permitted user or repository hooks. Convert and test their scripts as well as their configuration. See [Migrate hooks](/docs/agent-customization/migrate-customizations.md#migrate-hooks). > [!WARNING] > Copilot policy hooks run on the host, outside the session sandbox. Keep their scripts in administrator-controlled locations. Do not promote a repository hook to a policy hook while retaining a workspace-controlled script path; that would run editable workspace code outside the sandbox. See [policy hooks and sandboxed sessions](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-reference#sandboxed-sessions). Test failures and timeouts separately. The [Copilot command-hook reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-reference#exit-codes-for-command-hooks) documents timeouts as fail-open even for policy hooks. A requirement for complete audit coverage or fail-closed enforcement therefore needs more than the presence of a hook file. ##### Restrict hook sources Set `ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly` to allow hooks only from enterprise-managed sources and plugins that policy force-enables. Set `ChatStrictPluginOnlyCustomization` when you also need to block standalone user and workspace skills, agents, instructions, and MCP servers. Plugin distribution is a separate decision. To force-enable plugins or govern marketplaces across supported {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} clients, use the plugin controls in the [enterprise-managed settings reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/enterprise-administrators/enterprise-managed-settings#enabledplugins). #### Manage agent plugins and marketplaces Use the following policies to govern [agent plugins](/docs/agent-customization/agent-plugins.md) and customization discovery in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}: * `ChatEnabledPlugins` force-enables or force-disables named plugins. * `ChatExtraMarketplaces` adds plugin marketplaces. * `ChatStrictMarketplaces` restricts plugin installation to approved marketplace sources. An empty list blocks installation from all marketplaces. * `ChatCustomizationMarketplace` controls the unified **Browse** discovery surface. When disabled, marketplace discovery remains available in the existing customization management pages. * `ChatCopilotConnectors` controls connector discovery and whether connected connector MCP servers are available to {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} sessions. Plugins blocked by policy remain visible but appear disabled. In **Customize** > **Plugins**, policy-managed plugins are identified as managed by policy, and their toggles are locked. Marketplaces managed by policy are identified in the marketplace picker. For cross-client plugin governance instead of {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}-only policy, follow [Manage plugin marketplaces and plugins](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/administer-copilot/manage-for-enterprise/use-managed-settings/manage-plugin-marketplaces-and-plugins) to configure {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} enterprise-managed settings. Enterprise-managed plugin settings only require or block plugins. They don't set optional defaults. For optional project-specific plugins, use [repository defaults](/docs/agent-customization/agent-plugins.md#workspace-plugin-recommendations). Members can turn off these defaults unless managed policy requires the plugin. The enterprise-managed `strictKnownMarketplaces` setting also disables built-in marketplaces. Configure the permitted sources explicitly. #### Configure agent tool approvals Use {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} enterprise-managed settings to control session permission levels. Use {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} device policies for other approval behavior. ##### Manage permission levels For Copilot harness sessions, use enterprise-managed settings to control which permission levels developers can select and the initial level for new sessions. | Managed setting | Effect in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} | |-----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------| | `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` | Set to `"disable"` to disable **Allow all** in the permissions picker. | | `permissions.disableAssistedPermissionsMode` | Set to `true` to disable **Assisted permissions** in the permissions picker. | | `permissions.defaultMode` | Sets the initial permission level. Supported values are `"manual"`, `"assisted"`, and `"allow-all"`. | For example, start sessions with **Assisted permissions** when available, while preventing **Allow all**: ```json { "permissions": { "disableBypassPermissionsMode": "disable", "disableAssistedPermissionsMode": false, "defaultMode": "assisted" } } ``` If the configured default is unavailable, new sessions use **Manual permissions**. Setting a default doesn't prevent developers from switching to another permission level that the organization allows. In both the editor and the {% data variables.copilot.agents_window %}, supported permission levels restricted by policy remain visible but disabled. The picker shows **Disabled by policy** with a briefcase icon and an explanation. Unsupported permission levels aren't shown. These managed settings control [session permission levels](/docs/agents/run/approvals.md#permission-levels). The `ChatToolsAutoApprove` device policy controls global auto-approval separately. Refer to the [enterprise-managed settings reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/enterprise-administrators/enterprise-managed-settings) for configuration and deployment details. ##### Disable global auto-approval Set `ChatToolsAutoApprove` to `false` to prevent developers from enabling global auto-approval. While this policy is set, tool confirmations offer only one-time approval, and tool approvals that developers saved earlier aren't applied. > [!CAUTION] > Global auto-approval bypasses security prompts for tool invocations. Disable it unless your threat model explicitly supports this behavior. ##### Require manual approval for specific tools Use `ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval` to require manual approval for specific tools. For {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} harness sessions, a tool marked `false` removes **Allow all** from the permissions picker for the whole session. It does not require confirmation for each call to that tool, so **Assisted permissions** and saved session approvals can still approve it. ##### Configure terminal auto-approval Set `ChatToolsTerminalEnableAutoApprove` to `false` to turn off rule-based terminal auto-approval. For Local harness sessions, this policy does not prevent automatic approval of sandboxed commands or approval through session-level permissions. For {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} harness sessions, the policy requires approval for commands that run through the built-in shell tool. Set `ChatAgentHostCustomTerminalTool` to `false` to keep these sessions on that tool. Learn more about [tool approval](/docs/agents/run/approvals.md#tool-approval). #### Control GitHub Environments (Preview) [GitHub Environments](/docs/agents/run/remote-agent-sessions.md#github-environments-preview) provides continuity across supported {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} clients by registering an existing development machine for remote access. Administrators can control this registration and connection path to meet remote-access and data-handling requirements while allowing approved cross-device work. Set the `ChatAgentHostGitHubEnvironments` device policy to `false` to prevent sharing a machine as a GitHub Environment and discovering or connecting to other registered machines through this feature. The policy controls `setting(chat.agentHost.githubEnvironments.enabled)` and requires {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} 1.144 or later. Turning off {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} preview features through organization policy also forces this setting off. This control doesn't govern all remote connectivity. It isn't a blanket restriction on SSH or dev tunnels, and it doesn't configure other clients' policies. Review those access paths separately before treating it as an organization-wide remote-access boundary. ### Configure security and observability #### Configure agent sandboxing For {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} harness sessions, use the [session sandbox controls](/docs/agents/run/agent-sandboxing.md#control-sandboxing-for-the-current-session) and verify the [effective sandbox policy](/docs/agents/run/agent-sandboxing.md#inspect-the-effective-sandbox-policy) on the machine where commands run. The current [enterprise-managed settings reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/enterprise-administrators/enterprise-managed-settings#supported-keys) does not list the shared `sandbox` key as supported for {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}. For Agent Host sessions, use the [session sandbox controls](/docs/agents/run/agent-sandboxing.md#control-sandboxing-for-the-current-session) and verify the [effective sandbox policy](/docs/agents/run/agent-sandboxing.md#inspect-the-effective-sandbox-policy).
Sandbox device policies for Local harness sessions The following {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} device policies are deprecated and apply to Local harness sessions. They do not enforce sandboxing for Copilot harness sessions. | Policy | Local-session behavior | |--------|------------------------| | `ChatAgentSandboxEnabled` | Requires or disables sandboxing for supported terminal commands. | | `ChatAgentSandboxAllowNetwork` | Controls outbound network access for sandboxed terminal commands. | | `ChatAgentSandboxAllowUnsandboxedCommands` | Controls whether a command can run outside the sandbox after user confirmation. | Local harness sessions approve sandboxed terminal commands automatically. The [terminal auto-approval policy](#configure-terminal-auto-approval) controls rule-based approval, not sandbox auto-approval.
#### Configure agent network filtering Set `ChatAgentNetworkFilter` to `true` to restrict network access according to the allowed and denied domain policies. Use `ChatAgentAllowedNetworkDomains` for permitted domain patterns and `ChatAgentDeniedNetworkDomains` for blocked patterns. Denied domains take precedence. In Local harness sessions, network filtering applies to the fetch tool and Integrated Browser. In {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} harness sessions, these policies also apply to the Integrated Browser. When the `ChatAgentNetworkFilter` policy is `true` and the `ChatAgentAllowedNetworkDomains` policy contains permitted domains, {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} harness sessions block the runtime's web fetch tool from accessing domains outside that list, even with **Allow all** selected. This restriction does not require sandboxing. Terminal coverage depends on the selected harness, platform, and sandbox configuration. See [Configure sandbox network access](/docs/agents/run/agent-sandboxing.md#configure-network-access). Restart {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} after you change network filtering settings so new Integrated Browser sessions use the updated policy. #### Configure telemetry export with OpenTelemetry Use the `CopilotOtel*` policies to control [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) export for {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}. These policies cover export enablement, the collector endpoint and protocol, content and identity capture, the service name, resource attributes, and exporter headers. For the complete list of policies and the settings they control, see the [enterprise policy reference](/docs/enterprise/policies.md#vs-code-enterprise-policy-reference).
